## From committed data to a conditional decision

The capstone makes each transition inspectable:

**provenance → model choice → fit → residuals → parameter envelope → scenario**

- Eight committed Eyam observations, 18 June–20 October 1666.
- $N=261$ is the modeled population at the second-wave start.
- No render-time data download; the notebook has a deterministic fallback.

::: {.notes}
This is an educational workflow, not a new historical reconstruction. The
data and caveats are documented in data/README.md and the TOML provenance file.
:::

## Model and data caveats

We fit an effective transmission rate $\lambda=\beta c$ and removal rate
$\gamma$:

$$
\dot S=-\lambda SI/N,\qquad
\dot I=\lambda SI/N-\gamma I,\qquad
\dot R=\gamma I.
$$

The state columns are reconstructed from historical records and assumptions,
not direct measurements. A homogeneous closed SIR model omits rodent-to-human
transmission, household structure, movement, and reporting changes.

::: {.notes}
The effective lambda is deliberately not interpreted as separate contact and
per-contact transmission parameters; the sensitivity and identifiability chapter explains why.
:::

## Verify locally, then fit

```julia
metadata = TOML.parsefile("data/eyam_plague_1666.toml")
data = CSV.read("data/eyam_plague_1666.csv", DataFrame)
@assert bytes2hex(sha256(read("data/eyam_plague_1666.csv"))) ==
    metadata["csv_sha256"]
@assert all(data.S .+ data.I .+ data.R .== metadata["population"])

loss(θ, _) = sum(((predict(θ) .- observed_states) /
    metadata["population"]) .^ 2)
fit = solve(OptimizationProblem(
    OptimizationFunction(loss, AutoFiniteDiff()), [1.0, 0.5], nothing;
    lb = [1e-4, 1e-4], ub = [8.0, 8.0]), Fminbox(LBFGS()))
```

The normalized all-state least-squares objective is transparent, but it is not
a count likelihood.

## Fit diagnostics and deterministic envelope

```{julia}
#| label: fig-slide-ch12-fit
#| fig-cap: "Committed Eyam states, a fitted SIR trajectory, and residuals."
using CairoMakie
using CSV
using DataFrames
using OrdinaryDiffEq
using TOML

root12 = normpath(joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", ".."))
meta12 = TOML.parsefile(joinpath(root12, "data", "eyam_plague_1666.toml"))
data12 = CSV.read(joinpath(root12, "data", "eyam_plague_1666.csv"), DataFrame)
N12 = Float64(meta12["population"])
t12 = Float64.(data12.time_months)
y12 = permutedims(Matrix{Float64}(data12[:, [:S, :I, :R]]))
u012 = vec(y12[:, 1])
function rhs12!(du, u, p, t)
    λ, γ = p
    incidence = λ*u[1]*u[2]/N12
    du[1], du[2], du[3] = -incidence, incidence - γ*u[2], γ*u[2]
end
function prediction12(p)
    Array(solve(ODEProblem(rhs12!, u012, (first(t12), last(t12)), p),
        Tsit5(); saveat = t12, abstol = 1e-8, reltol = 1e-8))
end
grid12 = [(sum(((prediction12([λ, γ]) .- y12) ./ N12).^2), λ, γ)
    for λ in range(0.5, 6.0; length = 9)
    for γ in range(0.5, 4.0; length = 9)]
best12 = grid12[argmin(first.(grid12))]
fit12 = prediction12([best12[2], best12[3]])
res12 = fit12 .- y12
fig12 = Figure(size = (900, 650))
ax12a = Axis(fig12[1, 1], xlabel = "months since 18 June 1666", ylabel = "people")
for (j, label) in enumerate(["S", "I", "R"])
    lines!(ax12a, t12, fit12[j, :], label = "$label model")
    scatter!(ax12a, t12, y12[j, :], label = "$label data")
end
axislegend(ax12a, nbanks = 2)
ax12b = Axis(fig12[2, 1], xlabel = "time", ylabel = "model − data")
for j in 1:3
    lines!(ax12b, t12, res12[j, :], label = ["S", "I", "R"][j])
end
hlines!(ax12b, [0.0], linestyle = :dash)
fig12
```

Retaining nearby $\pm10\%$ parameter combinations gives a **scenario
envelope**, not a calibrated confidence interval.

::: {.notes}
Residual patterns are evidence about model mismatch, not just optimizer
quality. With eight reconstructed rows, formal uncertainty needs an explicit
observation model.
:::

## Decision comparison

Add $C$ with

$$
\dot C=(1-v(t))\lambda SI/N.
$$

Compare no policy with a one-month 50% reduction beginning at month 1, and
propagate the accepted parameter envelope through both scenarios.

- Validate $S+I+R=N$, finite trajectories, and lower modeled final incidence under the policy.
- Interpret the result as a model-based counterfactual under the chosen assumptions.

::: {.notes}
The final comparison is decision-relevant only after its assumptions,
parameter envelope, and data limitations are stated alongside it.
:::

## Takeaways and next steps

- A checksum verifies bytes, not historical truth.
- $\lambda$ is an effective rate; it does not identify $\beta$ and $c$.
- Residuals and sensitivity determine what conclusions are defensible.
- Better decisions require better observation and mechanistic models.

Read the [capstone chapter](../../chapters/15-data-to-decision-capstone.html),
[data provenance](../../data/README.html), and the
[CSV.jl](https://csv.juliadata.org/stable/) and
[Optimization.jl](https://docs.sciml.ai/Optimization/stable/) documentation.

::: {.notes}
Invite learners to replace one assumption at a time: an observation model,
household structure, or a different decision objective. The workflow should
survive that replacement even when the SIR model does not.
:::
